verdicts.name: GATE POWER AUDIT — 0 of 12 registered forward gates can discriminate
verdicts.n: 12 registered gates, re-powered from the study artefacts on disk
verdicts.stat: ADEQUATE: 0 of 12 · LR at the registered n: ridge 1.39 · sleeve 1.71 · 13D 1.62 · fund attribution 5.00 · deesc 3.81 · crash 14.5 · BASELINE mom 2.02 · bot 6.70 · OSINT 5.19 · RMT 1.96 · factor×regime 7.81
verdicts.note: power_audit.py asked of the published NEGATIVES: could the test have found the effect had it been there? This asks the identical question of the FORWARD GATES — the instruments rather than the results — and the answer is worse than the headline. A gate is ADEQUATE only if BOTH hold: LR ≥ 5 (a PASS multiplies your prior odds fivefold) AND P(false fail) ≤ 0.20 (power ≥ 80% at the registered alternative). NOT ONE OF THE TWELVE MEETS BOTH, and three of the four that clear LR ≥ 5 do so only by being NEARLY BLIND — P(false fail) 0.61 to 0.89. Nothing here lowered a bar; every redesign raises the required effect, adds a statistical requirement, or changes n and the observation unit. TWO DESIGN ERRORS PRODUCE THE 1.4:1. (1) THE ALTERNATIVE IS PLACED ON TOP OF THE THRESHOLD. Nine of the twelve gates read 'point estimate > B' with B set at or just below the pilot effect. When the alternative IS the bar, P(PASS | H1) = 0.5 identically, for every n — so more data fixes the false-PASS rate and NEVER touches the 50% false-fail rate. That is a design fact, not a data fact. (2) n WAS CHOSEN BY A CALENDAR, NOT BY A STANDARD ERROR: 4 cohorts, 6 months, 40 campaigns, 10 BASELINE months, 12 weekly logs, 200 events, 2 events — not one derived from n = (K·σ/Δ)². The ridge verdict is the sharpest case: criterion 1 alone gives LR 1.37 and criteria 2–3 contribute essentially nothing — the three-part rule is ONE COIN FLIP WEARING THREE HATS, n_eff 1.3, and it needs n_eff > 120 to be a real two-sided test. FIXABLE by redesign: de-escalation (this week, no extra calendar), bot regime gate (episode-clustered SE, n→40), 13D (null-rejection bar + SPRT, 2.9–3.8 yrs), shadow sleeve evidence half, OSINT 10th-factor, RMT (daily QLIKE/Diebold-Mariano), supply-chain CAR. UNFIXABLE on this data — relabel, do not run: ridge (three-branch with INCONCLUSIVE as the registered ~85% modal outcome), shadow-sleeve NAV gate (MONITORING; 9.8–14.4 yrs), ETF fund alpha comparison (65 YEARS at +3%/yr — the alpha claim comes out of the mandate and out of CONVICTION_STACK, and what is left is exposure-conformance plus a cost record), BASELINE momentum (no clock), crash reversal (reset), factor IC × regime (MONITORING, date removed). STANDING RULE PROPOSED: every gate registered from here carries the alternative as an effect size, the null and σ with its source, n from (K·σ/Δ)², the observation unit and its EFFECTIVE independence, LR and P(false fail) printed in the registration, and a pre-specified INCONCLUSIVE branch — or it is labelled 'monitoring, not evidence' in those words. A gate that cannot discriminate should not be dressed as a test.

verdicts.name: PERMUTATION NULLS — every frozen basket's p-value is ~10× too tight
verdicts.n: 12 graded events (3 DEESC in-sample, 9 ESC) × the 318-name frozen de-escalation basket
verdicts.stat: label-permutation null sd 0.025 vs empirical event-level null sd 0.404 raw / 0.260 sector-demeaned — a ~10× understatement
verdicts.note: A METHOD DEFECT WITH BOARD-WIDE REACH, filed separately from the basket it was found in because it is not about that basket. Shuffling TOP/BOTTOM labels destroys the very SECTOR TILT that makes a frozen basket risky, so a label-permutation null describes a random 159/159 split rather than the thing being tested. Measured against the ESC events — the closest available honest null — event-level dispersion is 0.404 raw and 0.260 sector-demeaned against the permutation null's 0.025. Sector demeaning recovers about half the overstatement; the rest is style and beta tilt. CONSEQUENCE: any p-value this project has published from a label shuffle on a tilted basket is anti-conservative, starting with the de-escalation basket's p < 0.002. Any frozen basket from here needs an EMPIRICALLY CALIBRATED null — a comparable set of real events the basket was not built from — not a label shuffle. Filed as a lesson beside 'a rule that exists only in a docstring is not a rule' and 'distrust your own guard'.

verdicts.name: DATE-ALIGNMENT FIX — one shared file, four studies, three reversals
verdicts.n: charts.json, 1,609 tickers: 866 monthly · 475 quarterly · 260 weekly · 8 daily
verdicts.stat: quarterly names kept 0 of 9,500 candidate stock-months (correct) · monthly 51,958 of 51,960 (100.0%) · weekly 12,605 of 13,903 · daily 65 of 239
verdicts.note: THE PARENT OF THREE OF TONIGHT'S RESTATEMENTS. charts.json monthly series are fetched range=max&interval=1mo, which Yahoo caps at ~168 bars, so P[k+1]/P[k] — read everywhere as 'the 1-month return' — was pooling 3-month, 1-month, 1-week and 1-day returns into one cross-section and annualising the mean ×12. THE SECOND BUG WAS PREVIOUSLY UNDOCUMENTED AND MORE DANGEROUS: a bar's close is its period-END close while its timestamp is the period START (AAPL's bar stamped 2025-12-01 closes at the 2026-02-27 daily close). So a naive 'just use the offs array' fix would have swapped an index error for a date error of the same magnitude. FIX: collapse each series to a calendar-month grid keyed by each bar's PERIOD-END month; resolve every window by month arithmetic; accept an N-month leg only if the target month exists AND lands within min(45, 15×|N|) days of the anchor shifted N months. Nothing is interpolated and no neighbouring bar is substituted — a name whose grid cannot support the window is DROPPED and the drop is counted. That quarterly names are eliminated wholesale is the cleanest evidence the filter does what it claims: a 12-1-1 window needs month k−1 and a quarterly grid never has it. OUTCOME: BASELINE momentum failed to replicate, low-vol withdrawn, param_stability reversed, score v2 unchanged and better supported. THE LESSON, filed: A SHARED DATA FILE IS A SHARED FAILURE MODE. Four studies written weeks apart failed the same way because all four trusted that a monthly array was monthly and none checked. Standing rule: any script that indexes a shared series POSITIONALLY must first assert the series' actual frequency, and the assertion belongs in the loader (00_lib), not in each consumer.

verdicts.name: MULTI-FACTOR JOINT REGRESSION — nothing is subsumed, and nothing is powered
verdicts.n: 7 sector-neutral factors · joint 28 months × ~443 names · deep price-only panel 132 months × ~903 names · 65,578-row panel
verdicts.stat: effective independent bets 6.34 of 7 · max VIF 1.55 · size +0.65%/mo per z (t=+2.40) · 0 of 7 factors adequately powered against their own literature benchmarks
verdicts.note: NOT A PRE-REGISTERED TEST and it has no authority to promote anything. It answers a structural question MODEL_CLASSES.md asked — 'every factor tested alone in decile sorts, so we can't say whether quality is disguised size' — and the answer is NO, to all of it. NOTHING IS SUBSUMED. Adding six controls moves momentum by +2%, quality by 12%, size by −23%. Quality is NOT disguised size: ρ = −0.114, quality keeps its sign and 74% of its magnitude under the control. Momentum and low-vol are NOT one bet: ρ = −0.125, and low-vol's coefficient moves 1% when momentum is added. PCA gives 6.34 effective independent bets out of 7 — momentum has its own component and shares it with nothing but the revision proxy. Almost all of the apparent movement between univariate and joint is SAMPLE, not subsumption. The single real subsumption relationship in the whole matrix is size → low-vol (ρ = −0.327, calm names are large names), and even there low-vol's residual survives. THE BAD NEWS THIS BUYS. 'Our factors are all secretly one bet' would have been a FIXABLE diagnosis for why every factor result is thin. It is not the diagnosis. The factors are distinct; they are individually very weak and mostly TOO WEAKLY MEASURED TO KNOW. Not one of the seven is adequately powered against its own literature benchmark in any specification: momentum needs 767–1,083 months, quality 789, size 8,747 (729 years). 0 OF 7 FACTORS PRODUCE AN INTERPRETABLE NEGATIVE — every null here is 'couldn't tell'. AND THE ONE 'SIGNIFICANT' RESULT IS THE BIAS. size +0.65%/mo per z is an implied D10−D1 of +2.27%/mo ≈ +31%/yr sector-neutral against a 0.15%/mo literature benchmark. It loses a third of its magnitude when the 153 speculative theme names are removed and falls below the bar when returns are winsorized. charts.json holds only survivors and the survivor distortion is largest at the small-cap end. The panel's own thermometer: the average stock-month returns +1.144%/mo = +14.6%/yr equal-weighted. THE SIZE COEFFICIENT IS THE SAME CLASS OF ARTIFACT AS THE WITHDRAWN LOW-VOL RESULT, and larger. It must not be read as a size premium and must not be traded. WHAT IT CHANGES: the collinearity objection to an XGBoost cross-section is answered and REMOVED — and replaced by a bigger one, because a gradient-boosted model on 28 cross-sections of a survivor-only universe has strictly more ways to fit noise and the same data underneath. The binding constraint is DATA, not model class: (1) a delisted-name price history — the single highest-value item in the whole research programme, (2) deeper balance-sheet history, (3) longer horizons, (4) then the non-linear model. Also usable now: the fund carries large implicit factor tilts it does not measure (§7) and they should be reported beside NAV.

verdicts.name: COMPONENT VaR — two implementations of one number (RESOLVED: amendment 19 applied 2026-07-29)
verdicts.n: same charts.json, 250 shared price days 2025-07-28 → 2026-07-27, 13 tail days at 95%
verdicts.stat: run_fund says GDX 44.59% top · risk_var.json says XLK 45.99% top · on IDENTICAL current weights both rank GDX first (44.59 log / 44.05 simple) · correct headroom to the 45% cap 0.95pp, enforcer sees 0.41pp
verdicts.note: RESOLVED — AMENDMENT 19 REGISTERED AND APPLIED 2026-07-29 (09_paper_fund/PREREG_AMENDMENT_19.md). run_fund.py's private re-implementation is deleted; the cap now imports and enforces risk_var.component_var_shares() at full precision (rounding to 0.1pp is a display choice and an enforcement threshold must not inherit one). risk_var.py is a REQUIRED PRE-STEP of rebalance and a stale artifact REFUSES the trade (`rebalance-refused`, no order) — refusing beats a silent inline recompute, which would hide the very failure the check exists to expose. risk_var.json is now stamped with the share vector, state_mtime_utc, prices and charts.json as_of. Applied alongside amendment 18 on the same file. The diagnosis below stands as the record of WHY. THE DISAGREEMENT WAS NOT METHODOLOGICAL — IT IS ENTIRELY A STALE WEIGHT VECTOR. risk_var.json is a 07-26 artifact describing a book that no longer exists (128.05 GDX shares, NAV $100,481, priced off a charts.json ending 07-21); the 27.62-share GDX MOC buy that filled 07-27 took GDX from 9.6% to 11.67% of NAV, and GDX has twice XLK's tail loss (−5.91% vs −2.93% on the 13 tail days). Every other candidate cause was tested and ruled out by holding the rest fixed: lookback window ~0, return frequency 0, correlation source 0, historical-sim vs parametric 0, cash in the denominator 0 (shares are scale-invariant, byte-identical), VaR definition 0 — both use the conditional expectation. ON THE RANKING run_fund IS RIGHT: GDX is the top contributor and the cap is about to bind on the correct instrument. DO NOT REDIRECT THE CUT TO XLK — XLK would need +18% with everything else static. ON THE METHOD risk_var.py IS RIGHT: run_fund builds its pseudo-portfolio out of LOG returns, but a portfolio return is a weighted sum of SIMPLE returns, so its decomposition sums to −1.66818% against the book's true ES95 of −1.62358% while risk_var's additivity gap is exactly zero. That is also the definition amendment 14 itself names — 'component VaR is measured the way risk_var.py already measures it'. THE ENFORCER DOES NOT IMPLEMENT THE AMENDMENT IT ENFORCES, and the error cuts GDX 0.24pp of NAV (~$239, ~3.2 shares) too deep at EVERY rebalance, in the same direction, on the instrument the cap always binds against. Correct trigger: GDX ≥ ≈$77.18 (+3.93%, ≈1.3 daily sigma on the 48.4% annualised vol the VaR window itself measures), not the ≈$75.51 the enforcer WOULD have fired at. ALL THREE REGISTERED FIXES ARE NOW IN run_fund.py: apply_risk_share_cap's private copy is gone and the cap is a policy layer over ONE measurement; risk_var.py is a required pre-step so its artifact cannot be stale at the moment of enforcement; risk_var.json is stamped with the state it describes. Two implementations of one risk number was the actual defect — the stale artifact was just how it surfaced.

verdicts.name: AMENDMENT 15 — vol target measured under stress correlations
verdicts.n: 354 drawdown days from the 10-year panel (fund_corr.json stress_days)
verdicts.stat: CURRENT, live from fund_corr.json 2026-09-03 01:06 UTC: calm 12.5% -> DRAWDOWN 21.2% against a 15.0% target · within_target True · required_scale 1.0 · STRESS_GOVERNS False, so NO scale-down is ever applied · invested 63.8% || SUPERSEDES the figure this board published until 2026-07-30: 'reported vol 10.3% -> 20.1% · target BREACHED · scale to 75% · invested 61.3% -> ~46%' (A15's registration, 2026-07-26) — which asserted a breach and a scale-down that STRESS_GOVERNS = False means the fund has never applied
verdicts.note: RESOLVED — measurement ON, governing OFF (option A, Riley's call). The stress figure is reported on every run and does NOT scale the book. THE DECISION STANDS. ITS STATED REASON DOES NOT, AND THE TWO MUST NOT BE RUN TOGETHER: STRESS_GOVERNS = False is not in doubt, is not reopened here, and now rests on a stronger argument than the one it was originally given. WITHDRAWN — named rather than deleted, per the register convention. Until 2026-07-30 this entry published, as A15's live justification and unpaired: 'across the 9-year panel the Sharpe barely moves, 0.40 unscaled vs 0.42 scaled'. That pair is retracted. NO SCRIPT IN THIS REPOSITORY COMPUTES IT — it lived in a measure_corr.py comment and in the note string that comment wrote — and PREREG_AMENDMENT_15.md makes no performance claim at all ('No performance claim.') while registering the OPPOSITE decision, SCALE-DOWN REQUIRED to 75%. It is also not a Sharpe ratio as constructed: a geometric numerator over an arithmetic sigma, with the scaled book's freed cash credited at rf 4.55% while the base book's own 38.6% idle cash is credited at 0%. Decomposed on the equal-weight five-ETF book those two artifacts are +0.289 and −0.233 — each roughly SIX TIMES their +0.055 sum, against the +0.020 A15 reported. The headline was the residue of two large mistakes nearly cancelling, and it moves 2–3× across a plausible range of the assumed cash rate alone. The companion figures in the same sentence do not reproduce either: the stated 'cost 1.18pt of CAGR (9.67% -> 8.49%) to buy 6.7pt of max drawdown (-27.4% -> -20.7%)' reconstructs as 10.59% -> 9.15% and -24.8% -> -18.6%. CURRENT — and it is an identity, not a statistic. Scaling every weight by k and holding the remainder at rf moves the book ALONG THE CAPITAL ALLOCATION LINE, and k cancels out of the Sharpe ratio exactly: (k*r+(1-k)*rf-rf)/sd(k*r+(1-k)*rf) = (r-rf)/sd(r). So the Sharpe difference from scaling is IDENTICALLY ZERO to machine precision (<=5e-16) at EVERY book size — measured on the 5 ETFs and on single-name books at N = 15/20/40 — and scaling down is a leverage choice rather than a risk improvement, by algebra, path by path, for any book or period. The levels were never measurable in any case: a 9-year panel resolves a Sharpe to roughly ±0.4, so neither 0.40 nor 0.42 is distinguishable from zero. 'Not no effect, not couldn't tell — nothing to tell.' Established by 04_research/STRESS_CORRELATION_SINGLE_NAME.md §2.2, §4; carried in fund_corr.json's own note since 2026-07-29. THIS BOARD WAS THE LAST LIVE CARRIER OF THE PAIR, because make_verdicts.py's hardcoded list was never corrected alongside measure_corr.py — the fix landed on the fund script and the research doc and missed the public page. The vol figures in this entry are now READ FROM fund_corr.json on every build instead of restated here. REVISIT CONDITION: external money or leverage, not a market move. Two other options were measured and rejected on evidence — a frequency-blended target gives 12.8%, still under 15%, so the 'on average' reading is ALREADY satisfied and no middle number changes behaviour; and reacting on detection is worse than it sounds, because the median drawdown episode has already fallen 14.4% before the signal fires (26.7% in 2020, with only 10.1% left to lose). Implementation note: the first version had ONE flag, so turning off the scaling would have turned off the measurement too. Split into STRESS_MEASUREMENT and STRESS_GOVERNS, because knowing the book runs 20.1% in a crisis is not an appetite question and should never have been switchable alongside one. ORIGINAL NOTE FOLLOWS. I proposed the wrong fix first and the measurement said so. After the deleveraging finding I suggested a stress-conditioned SHARE cap; measuring it showed that would have done nothing, because in DRAWDOWN the component-VaR shares CONVERGE (spread 35.6pt -> 31.3pt, top 41.8% -> 38.6%) and a 45% cap binds on nothing there. Concentration is a calm-state phenomenon. TOTAL RISK is the stressed one: at registration the same book, unchanged weights, ran 10.3% under the trailing window and 20.1% under DRAWDOWN correlations — an 89% increase, read at the time as a clear breach of a 15% target that never bound because it was estimated on ~81% calm days. THOSE TWO NUMBERS ARE THE REGISTRATION, NOT THE CURRENT BOOK. The live pair is in this entry's `stat` and is re-read from fund_corr.json on every build; the 15% target is currently WITHIN, not breached, and required_scale is 1.0. A third basis exists and is not the same measurement as either: the 8.96-year panel reconstruction in STRESS_CORRELATION_SINGLE_NAME §2.1 gives 10.81% calm / 20.48% drawdown, and A15's measurement half reproduces there exactly. Amendment 10's measured 0.227 average correlation was CORRECT and was the problem: 0.227 is a calm-state number and the book is not run in calm state alone. Under stress it is 0.549. THIS IS A RISK-APPETITE DECISION, NOT A CORRECTION. 'Target 15% vol' has two readings — 15% on average (the old behaviour, accepting ~20% in drawdowns) or 15% in all states (this, requiring a permanently smaller book). Implemented as the second because that is what the rule's own words claim, but it moves a quarter of the invested book to cash permanently and reverts with one flag. Fail-safe verified both ways: with the panel missing and with regime labels missing, it falls back to the trailing window and SAYS SO rather than printing a calm number under a stress heading.

Every study before this reported a single pooled number over a decade, and a pooled zero hides two completely different situations — a signal that was +0.06 then −0.06 (decay, possibly conditionable) and one that was flat zero throughout (absence). verdicts.name: DELEVERAGING RISK — amendment 14's cap is calibrated on the wrong state
verdicts.n: 2,259 labelled days · 1,827 CALM / 354 DRAWDOWN · fund 5 ETFs + 300-name universe
verdicts.stat: avg pairwise corr CALM->DRAWDOWN: fund 0.415->0.549 · universe 0.252->0.464 (nearly doubles) · risk-share spread 35.6pt->31.3pt
verdicts.note: The 'deleveraging' failure mode — synchronised selling collapsing diversification — measured rather than described. It is real: average pairwise correlation across 300 names goes from 0.252 in CALM to 0.464 in DRAWDOWN. A 1,600-name book is roughly half as diversified as it looks, in the state where that matters. THE PART THAT BEARS ON A LIVE RULE: amendment 14 caps component-VaR share at 45%, computed from the trailing year, which is overwhelmingly calm days. Recomputed by state, the shares CONVERGE under stress (spread 35.6pt -> 31.3pt) and — the uncomfortable bit — GDX's risk share FALLS from 21.9% to 16.7% while XLE's RISES from 20.6% to 26.3%. So the cap constrains the instrument that becomes relatively LESS dominant when it matters, and leaves alone the one that becomes more so. This does not invalidate amendment 14: as a normal-times concentration control it does what it was registered to do, and the registration says nothing about crises. But it should NOT be read as crisis protection, and the natural follow-up is a stress-conditioned version of the same cap. That is a new amendment and Riley's call. Measurement only — no weights changed. Note also the survivorship direction: the panel holds names listed today, so true crisis co-movement is understated and the convergence measured here is a LOWER bound.

verdicts.name: Cross-asset LEAD-LAG — the last untested structure
verdicts.n: 1,309 names · 16 sectors · 1,996 daily returns · 1.71m directed pairs deliberately NOT tested
verdicts.stat: gross +2.40bp/day t +0.88 · turnover 84%/day = 8.40bp cost · NET −5.99bp/day · 36% of months · decile rho +0.09
verdicts.note: Residual reversal asked whether a name reverts to ITSELF; this asks whether it FOLLOWS ANOTHER NAME — the last major structure the stack had not tested. 1,309 names give 1.71m directed pairs, so testing pairs individually would need |t|~5.5 and is the same trap that made pairwise cointegration indefensible. Instead ONE aggregate signal applied identically to every stock: leave-one-out mean of sector peers' PREVIOUS day, ranked cross-sectionally, long top decile short bottom. One hypothesis, one parameter set, nothing to correct for. The pre-registered prediction was 'gross weakly positive, net negative' and that is exactly what happened. Read the net t of −2.20 carefully: it is NOT evidence of an anti-signal, it is 84% daily turnover at 10bp round trip swamping a 2.4bp gross edge that was not significant to begin with. The decile means are flat from 0.01 to 0.04bp with rank correlation +0.09 — there is no ordering at all, so even the gross number is carried by extremes rather than by structure. VERIFIED, after the RMT study earlier today produced a clean null that turned out to be a non-converged optimiser: planting a lead-lag of known strength recovers it easily (k=0.05 → +14.48bp at t 5.28; k=0.20 → +50.63bp at t 18.14), so the null belongs to the data. verdicts.name: RMT covariance denoising — INCONCLUSIVE, not negative
verdicts.stat: RMT lower in 5/7 windows · 13.06% -> 12.94% realised vol (−0.9%) · paired t 0.61 · MDE 0.55pp vs a 0.13pp effect
verdicts.note: Marchenko-Pastur denoising: keep eigenvalues above λ+ = (1+√q)², replace the noise bulk with its average, preserving trace. Judged the only way that means anything — out-of-sample realised volatility of a long-only capped minimum-variance portfolio built from each matrix, walk-forward and PAIRED so both face the identical market path. Direction matches theory and matches the pre-registered prediction of a 'real but modest, single-digit' improvement: 0.9% less realised vol, lower in 5 of 7 windows. It does not clear |t|>=2. But the power calculation says the minimum detectable difference here is 0.55pp against an effect of 0.13pp — ~125 windows needed, 7 available — so this is INCONCLUSIVE, and calling it a negative would repeat the exact error the power audit found in five existing verdicts. TWO IMPLEMENTATION BUGS WERE FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE THIS NUMBER WAS TRUSTED, both mine: (1) a 504-day training window gave q = N/T = 3.17, a SINGULAR matrix that Marchenko-Pastur does not describe; (2) the optimiser ran a fixed 300 iterations and silently returned a near-equal-weight vector — in-sample vol 24.00% against equal-weight's 24.52%, versus 14.00% once converged — so the first run compared two identical portfolios and reported a null. It now returns a convergence flag and windows that fail to converge are skipped rather than counted.

verdicts.name: AMENDMENT 14 — risk-share cap at 45% of component VaR
verdicts.note: Companion to amendment 13, which exposed a concentration nothing guarded: rule 3 caps CAPITAL, and for a 43.7%-vol instrument that is a different quantity from RISK. GDX sat legally at its 19.0% half-Kelly limit carrying 59% of the book's downside, and the volatility target did not bind either at 14.0% against 15%. New rule 5: no instrument above 45% of component VaR, freed capital to CASH and not redistributed — the same convention rule 3 uses. 45% was chosen from a scan of 50/45/40/35/30 because it REPRODUCES the posture the fund already had (old book 45.8% top share; this lands at 45.0%). The intent is not to change how much risk is taken but to reach the same place by a stated rule instead of a side effect. Below 40% the cap stops controlling concentration and becomes de-gearing — 35% leaves the book 44% invested — which is a different decision and was not smuggled in here. Verified: fails OPEN and loudly when the price panel is missing (weights untouched, reason logged) rather than silently returning unconstrained weights; idempotent on repeat application so it cannot ratchet the book down across runs; monotone in the threshold. Known limitation, stated up front: with five instruments and no redistribution this converts risk into cash rather than diversification, so it is a blunt tool whose main effect is de-gearing.

verdicts.name: DETERMINISTIC REGIME — stable, and it still does not predict returns
verdicts.stat: stability kappa 1.000 (vs HMM 0.22) · Kruskal-Wallis on forward returns H 2.89 p 0.089 · STRESS holds 3.5% of days
verdicts.note: Third and final attempt on the regime overlay. A rule with no fitted parameters — 60d annualised vol >=25% is STRESS, 252d drawdown <=-10% is DRAWDOWN, else CALM, same 5-day confirmation filter. Thresholds are conventions (the textbook correction definition and the usual elevated-vol level), taken from outside the dataset so they cannot import training-window dependence; where they land in our distribution was reported, not tuned. Stability is perfect, kappa 1.000 — and the pre-registration said in advance that this proves nothing, because a CONSTANT label is also perfectly stable. The test that mattered was discrimination, and it fails: forward 21-day returns are not distinguishable across states (p=0.089), and STRESS is degenerate at 3.5% of days because DRAWDOWN is evaluated first and absorbs most high-vol periods. THE USEFUL DISTINCTION THIS PRODUCES: forward VOLATILITY is cleanly ordered (CALM 12.8% < DRAWDOWN 20.5%), so regime does carry RISK information — it is only RETURN information it lacks. That maps directly onto the live rule book: using regime to scale exposure or size risk has support; using it to modify expected return, which is what the REGISTERED TENSION x0.5 conviction modifier does, does not. Also worth noting DRAWDOWN windows show HIGHER median forward returns (+5.13% vs +1.59%) — the buy-the-dip direction, and not significant on 107 windows.

verdicts.name: REGIME K-SWEEP — retuning the state count does not fix it
verdicts.n: 663 shared days × K=2/3/4 · six full walk-forwards
verdicts.stat: kappa: K=2 0.342 · K=3 0.217 · K=4 0.127 — none reaches the 0.4 line, let alone 0.6
verdicts.note: Follow-up to the training-window instability finding, with the decision rule fixed before running (kappa >=0.6 stable, 0.4-0.6 marginal, <0.4 unstable). The 'fewer states are more stable' hypothesis is directionally correct — kappa rises monotonically as K falls — and nowhere near far enough. K=2's 79.8% raw agreement is the trap: both runs park ~80% of days in one state, so chance alone is 69.3% and almost all of the apparent agreement is arithmetic. RETUNING K IS A CLOSED AVENUE; the overlay needs replacing with a deterministic rule, not tuning. The sweep also reproduced the K=3 result independently (0.217 vs 0.24) from a different data path. Separately it found a defect in run_walkforward_10y.py that I wrote: the model object was not checkpointed, so every resume forced an unscheduled refit off the 21-day grid and the labels depended on where the run was paused. Fixed — checkpoints now only land on refit boundaries, making any chunking identical.

verdicts.name: REGIME DETECTOR — unstable to its own training window
verdicts.stat: best agreement under ANY relabelling 49.8% vs 33.8% chance · Cohen's kappa 0.24
verdicts.note: The walk-forward HMM read a price file starting 2021-12, so after a 500-day warmup it had 33 months of labels — 5 TENSION, 4 DRAWDOWN. Rerunning the IDENTICAL algorithm on the 10-year panel gives 97 months (30 TENSION, 43 DRAWDOWN) and, for the first time, a DRAWDOWN state that has actually seen the COVID crash. But the two runs agree on only 42.5% of the days they share, and the best any of the six state relabellings achieves is 49.8% against 33.8% by chance — kappa 0.24. Over the same 659 days one model spends 77% of its time in one state and the other spends 63% in a different one. Same features, same K, same confirmation filter; only the training length differs. This does not mean regime detection cannot work — it means these LABELS are substantially a function of how much history the model happened to have, and three signals plus the REGISTERED TENSION x0.5 modifier are conditioned on them. It also weakens stress_regime.py, which tested K=2/4 and ablations on the 33-month input and concluded the master variable survived: a stress test run on an underpowered sample is itself underpowered.

verdicts.name: POWER AUDIT — how many of our negatives are actually evidence
verdicts.stat: 4 REAL NEGATIVES · 5 INCONCLUSIVE (underpowered)
verdicts.note: A negative only carries information if the test COULD have found the effect. For each published negative: MDE = 2.80 x SE (the standard 80%-power two-sided 5% constant), compared against what the LITERATURE claims, never against our own estimate. Five of nine could not have detected the published effect if it had been fully present — their 'no' was the only answer available and should be read as INCONCLUSIVE, not as evidence of absence. Score v2 would need 737 formation years and has 10; accruals needs 186 and has 18. That is not an execution failure, it is a property of annual-formation cross-sectional tests, which is why the academic literature uses 50-90 year samples. The practical consequence: stop expecting annual-frequency factor studies to resolve on this data, and spend effort where n can actually grow. Two studies report only a t-statistic with no effect size and cannot be audited at all — itself worth fixing.
